- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >60.00), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% bias to first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >65.00 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 2–5% in next 5–7 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward in next 3–5 days.
